data.title: AI Infrastructure Demand Should Support Malaysia’s E&E Sector Into 1Q 2027
data.description:
CGS International expects Malaysia’s export growth to remain resilient into the first quarter of 2027, supported by sustained global demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-related semiconductor products and stronger energy exports, following a sharp acceleration in trade performance in October.

In its latest economic research report, CGS said Malaysia’s exports surged 61.1% year-on-year in October 2026, the fastest growth since April 2021, driven primarily by manufactured goods.

Manufactured exports rose 68.2%, led by electrical and electronics (E&E) products, metal products, machinery, equipment and parts.

E&E exports recorded particularly strong growth of 87.2%, reflecting robust AI-related demand and increased shipments to Singapore, the United States and Taiwan.

Meanwhile, mining exports expanded 37%, supported by higher shipments of metalliferous ores, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and crude petroleum.

Agricultural exports, however, contracted 6.1%, weighed down by weaker palm oil and rubber shipments.

Malaysia’s trade surplus widened to RM41.8 billion in October, bringing the cumulative surplus for the first 10 months of 2026 to RM274.8 billion, surpassing the full-year surplus recorded in 2025.

CGS noted that imports continued to grow rapidly, increasing 54.4% year-on-year in October, compared with 52.7% in September.

Intermediate goods imports surged 64%, reflecting continued demand for manufacturing inputs, particularly those supporting E&E exports.

Capital goods imports increased 32.9%, indicating sustained investment activity, while consumption goods imports grew 11.8%.

The research house expects imports to remain elevated through the remainder of 2026 and into the first quarter of 2027, supported by continued manufacturing and export activity.

CGS expects Malaysia’s E&E sector to remain the main driver of export growth, supported by the ongoing global semiconductor upcycle and investment in AI infrastructure.

Citing World Semiconductor Trade Statistics projections, the research house noted that global semiconductor sales are expected to expand by a further 29% in 2027.

With Malaysia’s domestic E&E capacity utilisation reaching 87.7%, CGS sees limited signs of a near-term slowdown in semiconductor shipments.

The research house believes strong demand for AI infrastructure and related investments should continue supporting Malaysian E&E exports into the first quarter of 2027, despite increasingly challenging year-on-year comparisons.

Beyond electronics, CGS expects energy-related exports to contribute positively to Malaysia’s trade performance.

Higher crude oil prices and sustained regional demand have supported petroleum shipments to Indonesia, the United Arab Emirates and Pakistan, alongside increased LNG exports to South Korea.

Resilient manufacturing activity in China and ASEAN is also expected to sustain regional energy demand into early 2027.

However, CGS cautioned that weaker crude oil prices could reduce the value of Malaysia’s energy exports.

Other downside risks include a sharper-than-expected economic slowdown in the United States or China, which could weaken global technology demand, and escalating protectionist trade policies that could disrupt international supply chains.

Despite these uncertainties, CGS maintained a constructive outlook, expecting Malaysia’s exports to remain on an expansionary path into the first quarter of 2027, with AI-driven E&E demand continuing to underpin the country’s trade performance.

data.title: Bitcoin Rebounds Above US$60,000, Ethereum Rises As Crypto Market Recovers From Sell-Off
data.description:
Bitcoin and Ethereum rebounded on Nov 23, recovering some ground following last week’s sharp cryptocurrency sell-off, although persistent market uncertainty continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

Bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, climbed 1.34% over the past 24 hours to approximately US$60,820 as of 10.15am Malaysian time, after trading between US$58,746 and US$61,648. Despite the recovery, Bitcoin remained 6.22% lower over the past seven days.

Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency, gained 1.53% to around US$1,713 as of 9.22am Malaysian time, having fluctuated between US$1,648 and US$1,733. However, it remained 5.85% lower over the preceding week.

The rebound followed a bruising week that saw Bitcoin plunge to approximately US$55,130, its weakest level since September 2024, amid widespread selling across cryptocurrencies and global financial markets.

Market sentiment remained fragile as concerns over elevated US Treasury yields, a potentially more hawkish Federal Reserve and weaker appetite for riskier assets continued to cloud the outlook.

While the latest gains offered some respite, investors remained cautious over whether the recovery could be sustained following the recent heavy losses.

data.title: Stock Today: Big Caring Holds At IPO Price In Morning Trade After Subdued Debut
data.description:
Big Caring Group Bhd shares remained unchanged at RM1.08 in morning trade, holding at their initial public offering (IPO) price following a subdued debut on Bursa Malaysia last week.

As at 10.39am, the retail pharmacy group’s shares were trading at RM1.08, with 17.46 million shares changing hands. The stock opened at RM1.07, touched an intraday high of RM1.09 and a low of RM1.06.

The counter’s last traded price was in line with its last adjusted closing price of RM1.08, while selling interest outweighed buying demand, with 5.36 million shares queued for sale at RM1.09 against 1.15 million shares queued to buy at RM1.08.

Big Caring made its Main Market debut on Nov 19, closing its first trading day at RM1.09, marginally above its IPO price of RM1.08.

The latest trading activity follows disclosures involving the group after its listing. On Nov 20, Big Caring revealed RM11.65 million in recurrent related-party transactions with Brego Life Sciences Sdn Bhd between Oct 1 and Nov 19, representing an aggregate percentage ratio of 2.6%.

The group said the transactions, which involved purchases and sales of nutraceuticals and medical devices as well as service-related dealings, were necessary for its daily operations and conducted on an arm’s-length basis.

Separately, filings showed that private equity investor Creador V LP’s indirect shareholding was reduced following IPO-related share disposals and an over-allotment arrangement. It retained a deemed interest of approximately 1.20 billion shares, equivalent to 16.287% of Big Caring’s issued share capital.

data.title: Gold Rebounds From 14-Month Low As Fed Rate Hike Bets Ease
data.description:
Gold prices rebounded on Monday after suffering their steepest weekly decline in eight months, with investors scaling back expectations of near-term Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

Bullion rose as much as 1.3% to around US$3,582 an ounce, recovering after a 9% slump last week that pushed prices to a 14-month low. Growing concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending also rattled global markets, triggering a sharp sell-off in technology stocks and prompting traders to reassess the outlook for US monetary policy.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that the Federal Reserve risked jeopardising the US economy by overtightening in response to the latest inflation data.

His previous attempt to rein in elevated long-term borrowing costs in August had pushed Treasury yields lower and sparked a brief rally in gold.

Swaps traders are no longer fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after Treasury yields fell across the curve on Friday. The policy-sensitive two-year Treasury yield ended the session 12 basis points lower, providing support for non-yielding bullion.

Gold has fallen by around a third since the US-Iran war erupted in late February, with higher energy costs fuelling inflation and prompting central banks to raise interest rates. The metal has also traded below the US$4,000 support level since Nov 11.

Spot gold rose 1.1% to US$3,578.24 an ounce at 8.26am in Singapore, while silver gained 2.6% to US$42.21 after tumbling 15% the previous week. Platinum and palladium also advanced.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index dipped 0.1% after rising 0.6% last week.

Bloomberg

data.title: Dollar Retreats From 19-Month High, Traders Scale Back Fed Rate Hike Bets
data.description:
The US dollar eased from a more than 19-month high in early Asian trading on Monday as investor confidence recovered following last week’s market sell-off, prompting traders to scale back expectations of aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve next month.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six major currencies, was flat at 103.80, retreating from its highest level since April 2025.

The euro gained 0.1% to US$1.0974, while the Australian dollar advanced 0.2% to US$0.6629. The British pound was flat at US$1.3091, while the New Zealand dollar held steady at US$0.5474.

Against the Japanese yen, the US dollar rose 0.2% to 158.63 yen as demand for the safe-haven Japanese currency eased.

Last week’s market rout had reduced expectations of a more aggressive Federal Reserve response to inflation, with futures markets no longer pricing in a 50-basis-point rate increase at the central bank’s Dec 8-9 policy meeting.

According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, fed funds futures reflected an 88.6% probability of a 25-basis-point increase and an 11.4% chance of rates remaining unchanged.

A week earlier, markets had assigned an 11.5% probability to a larger 50-basis-point increase, which has since been priced out.

However, Standard Chartered global head of foreign exchange, rates and credit research Eric Robertsen said the US dollar was expected to continue outperforming other major currencies.

He cited interest rate differentials, signs of stronger productivity gains in the US economy and a relative decline in political risk compared with countries such as France.

“If global risk aversion were to pick up, the USD should benefit as well,” he said.

Meanwhile, cryptocurrencies pared some of their rebound following Friday’s sharp decline, with Bitcoin slipping 0.1% to US$60,795.03 and Ether easing 0.2% to US$1,714.96.

Source: Reuters

data.title: Bursa Faces Another Week Of AI Fallout As KLCI Sinks Further
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its losses on Monday, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) falling for a sixth consecutive session as an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven sell-off continued to weigh on global equity markets.

The FBM KLCI shed 8.61 points to 1,547.90 in the opening minutes of trading, slipping below the psychologically important 1,550-point level as selling pressure spread across Asian markets.

Apex Securities said the local benchmark was likely to remain under pressure this week as Wall Street’s AI-driven sell-off deepened, with concerns over returns from AI infrastructure spending triggering further weakness in technology and semiconductor-linked stocks.

The research house said the S&P 500 had entered correction territory while the Nasdaq had erased its gains for 2026, reflecting a broader reassessment of valuations across the AI sector.

It added that a weak post-IPO showing from Anthropic, elevated inflation and a slower pace of central bank monetary easing had compounded the market downturn, which had spread beyond the US to Europe and Asia.

Apex Securities identified the FBM KLCI’s ability to hold above the 1,550-point support level as the key near-term test.

Meanwhile, TA Securities said increasingly oversold market conditions could encourage bargain hunting, with selected blue-chip stocks becoming more attractive following the recent sell-off.

Technology counters remained under pressure in early trading, with Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI) falling 38 sen to RM33.38, ViTrox shedding 28 sen to RM8.44, UWC declining 17 sen to RM5.26 and Cnergenz losing 13.5 sen to 99.5 sen.

Among actively traded stocks, Revenue gained one sen to 8.5 sen, while Dagang NeXchange (DNeX) slipped 1.5 sen to 40.5 sen and JCY International fell four sen to 43.5 sen.

Regional markets also faced heavy selling, with Japan’s Nikkei dropping more than 5% to 3,007 points and South Korea’s Kospi losing nearly 4% to 4,683 points.

However, US stock futures pointed to a potential rebound on Wall Street, with Nasdaq mini futures rising 2.7%, S&P 500 mini futures gaining 2.2% and Dow mini futures advancing 1.5%.

data.title: Ringgit Opens Higher On Stronger Trade Performance, US Dollar Gains Limit Upside
data.description:
The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Monday, drawing support from Malaysia’s stronger trade performance in October, although expectations of further monetary policy tightening in the United States continued to support the greenback.

At 8 am, the local currency traded at 4.1095/1150 against the US dollar, compared with last Friday’s closing rate of 4.1105/1150.

The stronger trade figures offered some support to the ringgit after the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) reported that Malaysia’s total trade surged 58 per cent year-on-year to RM436.6 billion in October 2026, from RM276.3 billion a year earlier.

The increase was driven by stronger growth in both exports and imports.

However, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit could remain under pressure amid growing expectations of further monetary policy tightening in the US.

“The yield curve flattening trade in the US Treasury suggests that bond market players are expecting the US Federal Reserve to be hawkish in their monetary stance.

“Hence, this will provide continued support to the US dollar in the near term,” he told Bernama.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the euro to 4.5094/5154 from 4.5113/5162 at last Friday’s close, while rising against the British pound to 5.3814/3886 from 5.3872/3931.

It also appreciated against the Japanese yen to 2.5857/5895 from 2.5886/5916.

Against regional currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.0978/1208 from 12.1179/1358 and gained against the Singapore dollar to 3.1864/1912 from 3.1882/1919.

It was unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah at 224.9/225.3 and the Philippine peso at 6.44/6.45.

data.title: Singapore Shares Face Heavy Opening Pressure, STI Falls To 4,914
data.description:
Singapore shares opened sharply lower on Monday, with the benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) falling 60.91 points, or 1.22%, to 4,914.26 as declining stocks significantly outnumbered gainers.

Market breadth was negative, with 201 decliners against 62 advancers as at 9.11 am, while total trading volume stood at 134.45 million shares valued at S$231.26 million.

Among the STI constituents, DBS Group Holdings fell 83 cents, or 1.26%, to S$65.28 as at 9.12 am.

Other actively traded blue chips included OCBC Bank at S$26.05, United Overseas Bank at S$35.13, Seatrium at S$1.51 and Singapore Telecommunications at S$4.12.

The broader market also saw weakness among real estate investment trusts (REITs), with CapitaLand Ascendas REIT slipping three cents, or 1.42%, to S$2.09.

Other REITs included Mapletree Logistics Trust at S$1.03, Frasers Logistics and Commercial Trust at 81.5 cents, Frasers Centrepoint Trust at S$2.10 and Keppel DC REIT at S$2.09.

The latest market figures indicate broad-based selling pressure across Singapore equities, with the STI falling below the 4,950-point level in early trading.

data.title: Stock Picks: Dagang NeXchange And Guan Chong
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Dagang NeXchange Bhd and Guan Chong Bhd as stocks with potential for further gains after both counters displayed bullish technical signals, supported by stronger trading volume and breakouts above key resistance levels.

In its technical analysis, RHB Research said Dagang NeXchange had staged a breakout after rebounding strongly from its recent low, forming its third consecutive bullish candlestick last Friday on its highest trading volume in six weeks.

The stock closed above the RM0.41 resistance and its 21-day simple moving average (SMA), indicating that bullish momentum was gaining traction.

RHB Research said further buying interest could lift the counter towards the next resistance levels of RM0.44 and RM0.47.

However, a fall below the RM0.38 support would invalidate the bullish setup and potentially trigger a correction.

Meanwhile, Guan Chong was also showing signs of an extended uptrend after reaching a fresh high.

The research house noted that the stock formed a long bullish candlestick last Friday and closed near its session high on strong trading volume. It also moved above the RM1.50 resistance, having breached its previous resistance level earlier.

With its 21-day SMA trending upwards, RHB Research expects the stock to advance towards RM1.60, followed by the next resistance at RM1.70.

On the downside, a drop below the RM1.40 support would signal a bearish breakout and raise the possibility of a correction.

Both counters are showing positive technical momentum, although RHB Research highlighted their respective support levels as key thresholds for monitoring whether the bullish setups remain intact.

data.title: Hang Seng Suffers Four-Day Losing Streak With AI Concerns Rattle Investors
data.description:
Hong Kong stocks suffered a sharp weekly decline, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index (HSI) losing 1,226.53 points, or 5.19%, to close at 22,410.80 on Nov 20, as mounting concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending and semiconductor industry weakness triggered a broad sell-off.

The decline wiped out the index’s brief 0.49% gain on Monday, leaving it lower for four consecutive sessions and more than 20% below its January peak, placing it in bear-market territory.

The HSI fell 1.03% on Tuesday to 23,508.18 before extending its losses by 0.91% on Wednesday to 23,294.76. Selling intensified on Thursday, when the index dropped 1.95% to 22,841.63, breaking below the 23,000 level for the first time in the week.

The benchmark ended Friday another 1.89% lower at 22,410.80, its weakest close in more than a year. The Hang Seng Tech Index plunged 3.78% to 3,511.14, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index fell 1.77% to 7,554.37.

Technology stocks were among the biggest casualties as investors reassessed the outlook for AI-related investments and the semiconductor sector, with uncertainty surrounding Nvidia adding to market caution ahead of and following its earnings announcement.

The sell-off gathered pace on Thursday, with Tencent Holdings plunging 6.55%, Alibaba falling 5.51%, Lenovo Group dropping 5.52% and Baidu declining 4.91%. Kuaishou also lost more than 4%.

Losses continued into Friday, although individual stocks showed some divergence. NetEase plunged 17.6% following a quarterly revenue decline, while Tencent slipped 1.26%. Contemporary Amperex Technology Co (CATL) fell 4.23% and Hesai lost 5.67%.

Alibaba bucked the broader market trend, gaining 3.48% on Friday following its earnings announcement.

The weakness reflected broader concerns across global technology markets, including uncertainty over the sustainability of AI-related capital expenditure and US restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips. These pressures added to investor caution towards technology-heavy markets.

The HSI’s weekly decline underscored the extent of the pressure on Hong Kong equities, with the benchmark ending the week below 23,000 after a brief early-week recovery failed to reverse the sustained selling.

data.title: Wall Street Suffers Sharp Weekly Sell-Off As Nasdaq Turns Negative For 2026
data.description:
Wall Street endured a bruising week, with the S&P 500 falling 6.82% as mounting concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investment and semiconductor industry weakness triggered heavy selling, pushing the Nasdaq Composite into negative territory for the year.

The S&P 500 shed 506.20 points to 6,910.39 for the week ended Nov 20, down from 7,416.59 on Nov 13. The index closed below the 7,000 level after suffering losses throughout the week, including a sharp 3.70% decline on Friday.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average also came under pressure, falling 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33 on Friday, while the Nasdaq Composite plunged 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73.

Technology stocks bore the brunt of the latest sell-off, with the Nasdaq’s Friday decline erasing its gains for 2026. The S&P 500 fell 2.02% on Thursday before extending its losses on Friday, while the Dow shed more than 1,100 points in Thursday’s session.

Investor sentiment remained fragile amid growing doubts over the sustainability of AI-related spending and the valuations of companies tied to the sector. Uncertainty surrounding Nvidia and concerns over US restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China added to the pressure on semiconductor stocks.

Nvidia was among the major casualties, falling nearly 10% on Friday amid reports of a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation into potential accounting issues. Semiconductor and other AI-linked stocks also faced heavy selling as investors reassessed their exposure to the sector.

The week offered little respite for investors. Although the Nasdaq managed a 0.42% gain on Wednesday, the S&P 500 extended its losing streak to five sessions before the broader sell-off intensified towards the end of the week.

data.title: KOSPI Plunges 7.95% In Worst Weekly Rout
data.description:
South Korean stocks suffered a steep weekly decline, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) falling 7.95% as mounting concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investment and semiconductor industry weakness triggered heavy selling by foreign investors.

The KOSPI shed 421.49 points to 4,869.96 for the week ended Nov 20, down from 5,291.45 on Nov 13. It closed below the 5,000 level for the first time since February, despite a brief recovery in the middle of the week.

The benchmark started the week with a 3.59% drop on Monday, followed by a 2.59% decline on Tuesday, which pushed it below 5,000 for the first time in nine months.

A two-day recovery then lifted the index by 1.99% on Wednesday and another 1.39% on Thursday, but the rebound proved short-lived as the KOSPI plunged 5.21% on Friday to 4,869.96.

The latest sell-off was broad-based, with all of the market’s 10 largest stocks by market capitalisation ending lower. Samsung Electronics fell 7.31%, while SK Hynix declined 6.59%. Samsung Electro-Mechanics recorded an even steeper loss of 12.5%, while SK Square and Samsung Life Insurance dropped 8% and 7%, respectively.

The weakness reflected growing investor concerns over the sustainability of AI-related spending and the outlook for semiconductor companies. Uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership and US restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China further weighed on sentiment.

Foreign investors were also a significant source of selling pressure during the week, particularly in technology shares, as concerns over the global AI sector prompted a reassessment of exposure to chipmakers.

The sharp weekly decline leaves South Korean equities under pressure, with the market’s near-term direction likely to remain sensitive to developments in the semiconductor industry and global investor sentiment towards AI-related stocks.

data.title: Singapore Stocks Sink 4.9% In Worst Weekly Decline Since April
data.description:
Singapore stocks suffered a sharp weekly decline, with the benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) losing 4.90% as mounting concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investment and semiconductor industry weakness triggered widespread selling across regional markets.

The STI fell 256.67 points to 4,975.17 for the week ended Nov 20, down from 5,231.84 on Nov 13. The index closed below the 5,000 level for the first time since June, extending its losing streak to five sessions before a brief rebound on Thursday.

The benchmark started the week with a 0.93% decline on Monday, followed by a 1.43% drop on Tuesday and another 1.06% fall on Wednesday. A modest 0.49% recovery on Thursday proved short-lived, with the index plunging 2.05% on Friday.

Friday’s sell-off was particularly broad, with 26 of the STI’s 30 constituents ending lower and none recording gains. Seatrium led the losses, tumbling 8.77%, followed by SATS, which fell 5.29%. Venture Corporation declined 3.32%, Singapore Exchange lost 3.14% and Keppel shed 3.07%.

Banking stocks also contributed to the week’s weakness, with DBS, OCBC and UOB among the counters sliding on Tuesday as selling pressure spread across the market.

The technology-led sell-off reflected growing investor unease over the sustainability of AI-related spending and the outlook for semiconductor companies. Uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership and US restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China further weighed on sentiment.

The decline was not entirely one-sided. Singtel advanced 2.5% on Tuesday, while the STI managed a modest recovery on Thursday despite weakness across regional markets.

However, the rebound failed to reverse the broader downturn, leaving Singapore equities with a difficult end to the week as global investors reassessed technology valuations and exposure to AI-related stocks.

data.title: Bursa’s Technology Stocks Take The Hardest Hit, MPI Leads Losers
data.description:
Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) suffered the steepest decline among Bursa Malaysia-listed stocks during this trading week, plunging RM2.74 to RM33.76 on Friday as technology and semiconductor counters bore the brunt of a broader market sell-off.

The semiconductor manufacturer topped the losers’ list on the final trading day after also appearing among the biggest gainers earlier in the week, highlighting the sharp swings in sentiment across technology stocks.

ViTrox Corporation Bhd was the second-biggest loser on Friday, shedding 59 sen to RM8.72, followed by Sunway Construction Group Bhd, which fell 58 sen to RM6.92.

Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd declined 42 sen to RM6.27, while UWC Bhd rounded out the five biggest losers after dropping 40 sen to RM5.43.

The weakness in technology counters was evident throughout the week, with MPI leading the decliners on Tuesday after losing RM1.90 to RM35.70. Kelington Group Bhd, MN Holdings Bhd and ViTrox also came under pressure during the session.

On the gaining side, KLCC Property Holdings Bhd led Friday’s advances, climbing 66 sen to RM8.88. British American Tobacco (Malaysia) Bhd followed with a 21 sen gain to RM3.30.

UMS Integration Ltd added 20 sen to RM6.20, while Axis Real Estate Investment Trust rose 19 sen to RM1.90. Allianz Malaysia Bhd completed the top five gainers, advancing 12 sen to RM19.

Nestlé (M) Bhd was among the more prominent gainers earlier in the week, leading the advances on Monday and Tuesday before reversing course on Wednesday. It also ranked among the joint top gainers on Thursday, reflecting mixed trading in selected heavyweight consumer counters.

The week’s trading also showed a marked deterioration in overall market breadth. On Friday, decliners overwhelmed gainers by 837 to 325, while 444 counters were unchanged, 1,234 untraded and 32 suspended.

This compared with Monday’s 673 decliners against 375 gainers, although market breadth briefly turned positive on Wednesday, when 630 counters advanced against 430 that declined.

Trading activity picked up towards the end of the week, with turnover rising to 3.64 billion shares valued at RM2.99 billion on Friday, from 3.06 billion shares worth RM2.76 billion a day earlier.

The combination of heavier trading and a wide gap between losers and gainers underscored the extent of selling pressure, particularly in technology-related counters, as Bursa Malaysia ended the week at a 15-month low.

data.title: Bursa’s Brief Rebound Fizzles Out As KLCI Loses 26 Points
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended this trading week sharply lower, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shedding 26.08 points, or 1.65%, to 1,556.51 as persistent selling in heavyweight counters and a global technology sell-off weighed on investor sentiment.

The index closed below the 1,560 level after falling for four consecutive sessions, touching a 15-month low on Friday. Its weekly decline came despite a modest rebound at the start of the week, when the benchmark gained 5.44 points, or 0.34%, to 1,588.03 on Nov 16.

Selling pressure returned on Tuesday, with the FBM KLCI losing 12.88 points, or 0.81%, to 1,575.15 as technology and data-centre stocks came under pressure amid concerns over Nvidia and tighter US licensing requirements for advanced AI chip exports.

The benchmark extended its losses on Wednesday, dropping another 8.42 points, or 0.53%, to 1,566.73. Banking and plantation heavyweights weighed on the index, offsetting gains among selected technology counters.

The market showed signs of stabilisation on Thursday, when the FBM KLCI slipped just 0.57 points to 1,566.16, despite falling as much as 10.2 points during the session.

However, selling resumed on Friday, dragging the index down 9.65 points, or 0.62%, to 1,556.51. It traded between 1,548.67 and 1,559.11, marking its lowest level in 15 months.

The weakness mirrored a broader sell-off across global equity markets, particularly in technology and semiconductor stocks, as investors grew increasingly cautious over the outlook for AI-related investments and Nvidia’s position in the industry.

Technology and data-centre counters remained under pressure throughout the week, while banking and plantation heavyweights added to the FBM KLCI’s losses on Wednesday.

The market’s performance reflected a difficult week for regional equities, with uncertainty surrounding US export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China and concerns over technology valuations weighing on risk appetite.

The FBM KLCI’s decline extended its recent losing streak, leaving the benchmark more than 26 points lower than its Nov 13 close of 1,582.59.

data.title: Bitcoin Slides To Lowest Level In Two Years Amid Market Sell-Off
data.description:
Bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency by market value, fell to its lowest level in two years on Friday, dropping below US$56,000 as concerns over stretched artificial intelligence (AI) stock valuations triggered a broader sell-off in risk assets.

The cryptocurrency slid 5.10% to US$55,830 at 11:13 pm ET on Friday (4:13 am GMT on Saturday), marking its lowest level since September 2024. It had earlier declined 3.57% to US$56,813.68, after falling below the US$60,000 mark for the first time since July.

The latest decline comes amid growing investor concerns over the profitability of massive AI infrastructure investments, alongside rising borrowing costs and regulatory uncertainty following the Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections.

Markets were also unsettled by developments involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, adding to pressure on technology-related and other risk-sensitive assets.

The broader US stock market was heading towards its steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when President Donald Trump announced his “Liberation Day” tariffs, underscoring the extent of investor caution.

Bitcoin’s latest slide highlights its vulnerability to broader market sentiment, as uncertainty surrounding technology valuations and economic conditions weighs on demand for riskier investments.

data.title: Taiwan Stocks Record Third Largest Single Day Decline As Tech Rout Hits TSMC
data.description:
Taiwan stocks plunged 6.23 percent on Friday, shedding 2,393.6 points in their third-largest single-day decline on record, as the benchmark index extended its losses for the week to more than 7,600 points.

The weighted index closed at 36,033.29 points, with turnover reaching 877.35 billion New Taiwan dollars (26.62 billion U.S. dollars). It fell 7,641.83 points, or 17.5 percent, over the week.

Heavyweight stocks led the sell-off. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) fell 4.76 percent to 2,000 New Taiwan dollars, while Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. dropped 4.76 percent to 210 New Taiwan dollars.

MediaTek Inc. plunged to its daily 10-percent limit at 3,350 New Taiwan dollars, while Delta Electronics also hit the daily limit, closing at 900 dollars.

All eight major stock categories ended lower. Plastics and chemicals stocks recorded the steepest decline, falling 8.42 percent, followed by machinery and electrical equipment stocks, down 6.29 percent, and cement and ceramics stocks, declining 6.27 percent. Financial stocks, meanwhile, lost 5.82 percent.

Only 16 stocks advanced, while more than 1,000 declined, accounting for over 90 percent of listed shares.

The latest sell-off came just days after the benchmark index on Nov. 16 posted its second-largest single-day closing-point loss on record.

Financial analysts said the market rout reflected deeper structural vulnerabilities in Taiwan’s economy, including its heavy reliance on the semiconductor and other technology industries, and the uneven distribution of gains from the artificial intelligence boom.

data.title: Hong Kong Stocks Sink 1.89% As Hang Seng Enters Bear Market
data.description:
Hong Kong stocks extended their losses on Friday, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index (HSI) falling 1.89% to its lowest closing level in more than a year as concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending and semiconductor industry weakness triggered another broad sell-off.

The HSI dropped 430.82 points to 22,410.80, marking its fourth consecutive session of losses and its lowest close since April 30, 2025. The index also briefly fell as much as 2.2% during the session, bringing its decline from the Jan 29 peak to 20%, the threshold for a bear market.

Technology stocks bore the brunt of the selling, with the Hang Seng Tech Index plunging 3.78% to 3,511.14. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index, which tracks mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong, fell 1.77% to 7,554.37.

Investor concerns over the sustainability of AI investment weighed on technology and semiconductor counters, extending a regional sell-off following sharp losses on Wall Street.

NetEase was among the biggest drags, plunging 17.6% after reporting a quarterly revenue decline. Tencent Holdings fell 1.26% to HK$344, its lowest level in more than two years, amid concerns over the impact of AI-related spending on margins.

Other notable decliners included battery maker CATL, which fell 4.23%, and lidar manufacturer Hesai, down 5.67%. Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing also lost more than 3%.

Alibaba-W bucked the broader weakness, rising 3.48% following its earnings announcement.

Trading activity picked up, with market turnover reaching HKD270.3 billion. Meanwhile, southbound net buying stood at HKD11.811 billion, indicating that mainland investors continued to add exposure selectively despite the broader market weakness.

The latest decline extended a difficult week for Hong Kong equities, with the HSI having already fallen below the 24,000 level earlier in the week.

data.title: Nasdaq Suffers Worst Week Since 2020 As AI Sell-Off Deepens
data.description:
Wall Street suffered another sharp sell-off on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average into correction territory as growing concerns over artificial intelligence valuations and heavy technology spending rattled investors.

The S&P 500 fell 265.41 points, or 3.70 per cent, to 6,910.42, while the Dow dropped 949.73 points, or 1.93 per cent, to 48,147.33. The Nasdaq Composite suffered the steepest decline, shedding 1,261.47 points, or 5.28 per cent, to 22,617.73.

Both the S&P 500 and Dow closed more than 10 per cent below their record highs, confirming corrections. The S&P 500 also recorded its seventh consecutive daily decline, its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The Nasdaq’s weekly decline was its largest since March 2020, while the index slipped into negative territory for the year. The S&P 500 and Dow also recorded their biggest weekly percentage losses since April 2025.

The sell-off intensified following a disappointing second trading session for artificial intelligence company Anthropic, whose shares fell 9.1 per cent after debuting on Thursday. Nvidia plunged 13.8 per cent, while Amazon and Meta Platforms lost 3.9 per cent and 5.9 per cent respectively.

Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management, said market sentiment was outweighing underlying economic fundamentals and corporate earnings.

The CBOE Volatility Index, Wall Street’s so-called fear gauge, climbed to its highest closing level since April 7, 2025.

Elsewhere, Intuit fell 12.8 per cent after cutting its annual revenue growth forecast, while Caterpillar declined 5 per cent amid concerns over demand for its power-generation equipment.

Cryptocurrency-related stocks also weakened after Bitcoin fell below US$60,000, with Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood losing between 6.3 per cent and 9.6 per cent.

data.title: KOSPI Plunges 5.21% To 10-Month Low In AI Sell-Off
data.description:
South Korean stocks suffered a sharp sell-off on Friday, with the benchmark KOSPI plunging 5.21 per cent to its lowest level in 10 months as mounting concerns over artificial intelligence investments and semiconductor demand rattled investors.

The index fell 267.93 points to close at 4,869.96, its weakest finish since Jan 16, when it ended at 4,840.74. The decline came after another steep loss in the previous session, extending pressure on the country’s technology-heavy market.

Selling intensified during the morning, prompting the Korea Exchange to activate a sell-side sidecar at 11.54 am, suspending program trading for five minutes after the KOSPI fell 4.54 per cent to 4,904.69.

Chipmakers led the losses, with Samsung Electronics plunging 7.31 per cent to KRW182,500, while SK Hynix dropped 6.59 per cent to KRW1.105 million. Samsung Electro-Mechanics also tumbled 12.5 per cent, while SK Square fell 8 per cent.

All of the market’s 10 largest companies by market capitalisation ended lower.

The sell-off reflected wider concerns over the sustainability of massive artificial intelligence infrastructure investments, with Anthropic’s strong stock market debut failing to reassure investors about the sector’s growth prospects.

Foreign investors also added to the pressure, recording net sales of more than KRW1.11 trillion in KOSPI-listed shares, according to Korea Exchange data.

The weakness extended to the technology-heavy KOSDAQ, which fell nearly 4.9 per cent during the session, highlighting the broader retreat from South Korean equities amid the global AI-led market downturn.
